items.target: あしたのくじからです
items.reviewNote: EXERCISES V model answer, lifted verbatim, split from kaigi-itsu-q. Particle job: の (no) linking a day to an hour, the pattern GRAMMAR 3 exists to teach.
items.note: GRAMMAR 3: the larger unit leads. あした (ashita) comes first, then the hour, joined by の (no).
items.scene: answering when the meeting is

items.target: かいぎはさんじですか
あしたです
items.reviewNote: Constructed answer to yasumi-itsu-q. Every existing いつ answer in the deck gives an hour, so the learner has never seen いつ answered with a day alone, which is half of what the question is for.
items.note: いつですか (itsu desu ka) can be answered with a day on its own — it does not demand a clock time the way なんじですか (nan-ji desu ka) does.
items.scene: answering when the day off is

items.target: ばんごはんはろくじからです
items.reviewNote: Constructed from EXERCISES VI item 1 (ばんごはん, 6:00). Vocabulary job: ばんごはん (bangohan) is chapter vocabulary that arrives as a word card only in the wave-1 proposal — this is its first and only use in a sentence.

items.target: ごごはちじまでです
items.reviewNote: Constructed answer to depaato-nanji-made-q, from the book's own 8:00 cue in EXERCISES III-B, made explicit as P.M. Adds a second ごご (gogo) sentence to the lesson.
items.scene: answering what time the department store closes

items.target: いまくじいっぷんです
items.note: Combines くじ (kuji), the irregular '9 o'clock' reading (く/ku, not きゅう/kyū) seen in ごごくじ (gogo kuji), with いっぷん (ippun), the irregular '1 minute' reading from earlier in this lesson.

items.target: なんじまでですか
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue, Smith's follow-up. Collides in family with the existing fib-c3-meeting-end-q (かいぎはなんじまでですか), but this is the topicless follow-up form, which the deck never shows — in a real exchange you drop the topic on the second question. Marked medium so it is easy to prune if that feels too close.
items.scene: no topic named — you already asked about lunchtime

items.target: いまくじじゃありません
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form job: member 2 of the contrast set. No card in the deck negates a time, so the learner has no model for saying a clock reading is wrong.
items.note: じゃありません (ja arimasen) negates a time exactly as it negates a noun in これはとけいじゃありません (kore wa tokei ja arimasen) from Lesson 2. Member 2 of the set begun by いまくじです (ima ku-ji desu).

items.note: いつ (itsu) asks which day the meeting is; なんじ (nan-ji) asks for the clock hour instead, as in きょうのかいぎはなんじですか (kyō no kaigi wa nan-ji desu ka), 'What time is today's meeting?' — that one already assumes you know the day.

items.target: ラストオーダーはにじです
items.reviewNote: Constructed from the Target Dialogue's closing exchange. Form job: apart from いま (ima) sentences, the deck has no 〜は timeです statement at all — every event card uses から or まで, so the simplest form of the pattern is missing.
items.note: Plain です (desu) pins an event to one moment. からです (kara desu) would mean it opens then and carries on, as in ジムはごぜんくじからです (jimu wa gozen ku-ji kara desu).

items.pronunciation: jimu wa nanji kara nanji made desu ka
items.note: から (kara, 'from') and まで (made, 'to/until') bracket a range — here a time range, but the same から〜まで (kara~made) pattern works for places and dates too.

items.reviewNote: Constructed, using the book's own cast. Particle job: の (no) in its Lesson 1 possessive sense combined with this lesson's いつ (itsu) question — no card puts a person and an event's timing in one sentence.
items.note: Two jobs for の (no) sit side by side in this lesson: possession in スミスさんのプレゼン (sumisu san no purezen) and time-linking in あしたのくじ (ashita no ku-ji).

items.pronunciation: resutoran wa nan-ji made desu ka.
items.reviewNote: EXERCISES IV-B model dialogue, verbatim. Included mainly to carry its answer, which is the only ごご (gogo) sentence in the chapter. Same family as the existing fib-c3-meeting-end-q, but with a different topic and a P.M. answer.

items.target: しちじからです
items.reviewNote: EXERCISES VI, the front desk's reply, split from hotel-asagohan-q. Also the deck's only sentence use of しちじ (shichi-ji).
items.scene: answering what time breakfast starts

items.target: とうきょうはいまごごよじはんです
items.pronunciation: tōkyō wa ima gogo yo-ji han desu.
items.reviewNote: Constructed from SPEAKING PRACTICE 1, where Tokyo is 4:30 and London is 8:30 A.M. Particle job: は (wa) over a geographical topic had a single example, and this gives it a ごぜん/ごご minimal pair on the same clock moment.
items.note: GRAMMAR 1: naming another place makes it the topic with は (wa), as in ロンドンはいまなんじですか (rondon wa ima nan-ji desu ka) earlier in this lesson. That question's answer, ごぜんはちじはんです (gozen hachi-ji han desu, '8:30 A.M.'), is the same moment as this one but the opposite half of the day.

items.english: Excuse me. What time does breakfast start?
items.target: すみません。あさごはんはなんじからですか
items.pronunciation: sumimasen. asagohan wa nan-ji kara desu ka.
items.reviewNote: EXERCISES VI model dialogue (Smith asking the hotel front desk) — a section that produced no cards. This is the second and last 〜はなんじからですか example; it is the practical one the book flags in Active Communication ('ask about the business hours of a facility').

items.target: はい、くじです
items.reviewNote: Constructed answer to ima-kuji-desu-ka. Form job: the はい、〜です reply shape from Lesson 1 (はい、アメリカじんです) has never been applied to a time.
items.scene: answering yes to whether it is 9:00 now

items.target: ぎんこうはごぜんくじからです
items.pronunciation: ginkō wa gozen ku-ji kara desu.
items.reviewNote: Constructed from EXERCISES IV-A item 2 (ぎんこう, 9:00). Particle job: から (kara) with a Lesson 1 noun the lesson explicitly re-uses; ぎんこう (ginkō) has had no sentence of its own since it was introduced.

items.target: こちらはみせのひとです
items.pronunciation: kochira wa mise no hito desu.
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: ひと (hito) and みせのひと (mise no hito) exist only as bare word cards. Uses Lesson 1's こちらは… introduction frame, so no grammar beyond what the learner has.
items.note: の (no) joins みせ (mise) to ひと (hito) the same way it joins a company to a person in こちらはのぞみデパートのたなかさんです (kochira wa nozomi depāto no tanaka san desu) from Lesson 1.

items.target: にじです
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue, split from td-last-order-q. English collides with the existing vocabulary card ni-ji ('2:00, two o'clock') — this one carries a hint; ni-ji should get one too (e.g. 'the bare clock time') if the owner wants both reachable cleanly.
items.scene: answering what time the last order is

items.target: ろっぷん
items.note: Irregular reading for '6 minutes' — ろく (roku) becomes ろっ (rop) before ふん (fun), not ろくふん (rokufun).

items.english: Excuse me. What time does lunchtime start?
items.target: すみません。ランチタイムはなんじからですか
items.pronunciation: sumimasen. ranchitaimu wa nan-ji kara desu ka.
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue, Smith's first question. The deck has no 〜はなんじからですか question at all, only the まで version (fib-c3-meeting-end-q), so the opening-time question is a complete gap. Verbatim from the book, including the すみません (sumimasen) opener that makes it usable with a stranger.

items.english: It's open from 7:00 A.M. to 11:00 P.M.
items.target: ごぜんしちじからごごじゅういちじまでです
items.pronunciation: gozen shichi-ji kara gogo jūichi-ji made desu.
items.reviewNote: Constructed answer to furonto-q. Form job as well as vocabulary: this is the only sentence in the lesson carrying both ごぜん and ごご, which is where their placement before the hour actually matters.
items.note: ごぜん (gozen) and ごご (gogo) each sit in front of their own hour, so a span can cross midday without any extra word.
items.scene: answering the reception desk's opening hours

items.target: しごとはごじまでです
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle job: the second half of the から/まで minimal pair. Every other から card and まで card in the deck uses a different topic, so the particle itself was never the variable.
items.note: The same sentence as しごとはくじからです (shigoto wa ku-ji kara desu) with one thing changed: から (kara) marks where a stretch of time begins, まで (made) where it ends.

items.target: コンサートはきょうのろくじからです
items.pronunciation: konsāto wa kyō no roku-ji kara desu.
items.reviewNote: Constructed from EXERCISES V item 3 (コンサート, きょうの6じ). Vocabulary job: コンサート (konsāto) had no sentence; written as a statement rather than another いつですか pair so the frame is not repeated a third time.

items.target: いまなんじですか
items.reviewNote: EXERCISES II model dialogue (also SPEAKING PRACTICE 1). This is the question the lesson is named after and it is missing from the deck entirely — the deck has いまさんじです (the answer) but never the question.
items.note: No topic is needed when asking the current time — GRAMMAR 1 notes that the present time takes no subject, and いま (ima) is simply added adverbially.

items.target: ごごじゅういちじまでです
items.reviewNote: EXERCISES IV-B model answer, split from resutoran-nanji-made-q. ごご (gogo) existed only as a bare word and in the bare time ごごくじ — this is its first appearance inside a sentence, which is where the word-order point actually bites.
items.note: ごぜん (gozen) and ごご (gogo) go before the hour, the opposite of English A.M./P.M.
items.scene: answering what time the restaurant closes

items.target: じゅっぷん
items.note: Irregular reading for '10 minutes' — じゅう (jū) becomes じゅっ (jup) before ふん (fun); じっぷん (jippun) is an accepted alternate reading.
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-2) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: Lesson 3 teaches the ...fun minute counter

items.target: パーティーはしちじからじゅうじまでです
items.pronunciation: pātī wa shichi-ji kara jū-ji made desu.
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: パーティー (pātī) appears in the deck only with いつ (itsu) and never with clock times, so the learner never sees an event given a span rather than a start.

items.target: いいえ、さんじじゃありません
items.scene: answering whether the meeting is at 3:00

items.english: What time does the department store close?
items.target: デパートはなんじまでですか
items.pronunciation: depāto wa nan-ji made desu ka.
items.reviewNote: Constructed from EXERCISES III-B and IV-A, which both re-use デパート (depāto). Vocabulary job: デパート is a Lesson 1 word that this lesson leans on but that has had no sentence of its own since Lesson 1.

items.english: What time is the reception desk open, from and to?
items.target: フロントはなんじからなんじまでですか
items.pronunciation: furonto wa nan-ji kara nan-ji made desu ka.
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: フロント (furonto) appears in the chapter only as a speaker label in EXERCISES VI, never inside a sentence, so the learner meets the word but never uses it.

items.target: くじからです
items.reviewNote: Constructed answer to mise-nanji-kara-q, split per the Q/A rule. Elliptical in both languages, so the hint names the question without leaking the hour.
items.scene: answering what time the shop opens

items.english: The presentation is from 10:00 A.M. tomorrow.
items.target: プレゼンはあしたのごぜんじゅうじからです
items.pronunciation: purezen wa ashita no gozen jū-ji kara desu.
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle job: の (no) between time expressions had three examples, all day + plain hour. This is the only one where a ごぜん/ごご word sits inside the の phrase, which is where learners tend to put の in the wrong place.
items.note: Three time words stack biggest first — あした (ashita), then ごぜん (gozen), then the hour — and only the day takes の (no).

items.target: いちじからさんじまでです
items.reviewNote: EXERCISES IV-C model answer, split from kaigi-nanji-kara-made-q. English mirrors the existing fib-c3-lunch-break-a wording but with different times, and the hint names a different question, so the two stay distinguishable.
items.scene: answering what hours the meeting runs

items.target: にじはんからです
items.reviewNote: Constructed answer to kyou-no-kaigi-nanji-q. Also puts 〜はん (han) into a short から reply, a shape the deck only has at 11:30 and 4:30.
items.scene: answering what time today's meeting is

items.english: What time does the restaurant open?
items.target: レストランはなんじからですか
items.pronunciation: resutoran wa nan-ji kara desu ka.
items.reviewNote: Constructed from EXERCISES IV-A item 1 (レストラン). Particle job: the から/まで contrast in question form on a single topic — the deck's から questions and まで questions all sit on different nouns, so the contrast is never visible.
items.note: Minimal pair with レストランはなんじまでですか (resutoran wa nan-ji made desu ka): swapping から (kara) for まで (made) is the whole difference between asking when a place opens and when it shuts.

items.target: よんぷん
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-2) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: Lesson 3 teaches the ...fun minute counter

items.target: いまくじですか
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form job: member 3 of the contrast set, and the deck's only yes/no か question in this lesson — every other か card is an information question.
items.note: Member 3 of the set: か (ka) turns いまくじです (ima ku-ji desu) into a yes/no question, unlike なんじですか (nan-ji desu ka), which asks for the time itself.

items.target: にじはんまでです
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue, the shop's reply, split from td-lunchtime-end-q. English matches the book's own gloss and drops the topic exactly as the Japanese does.
items.scene: answering what time lunchtime ends

items.target: いまくじです
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form job: opens the affirmative / negative / question contrast set. The negative and the yes/no question come from Lessons 1–2, and this lesson never re-applies them to a time, so the set is assembled here.
items.note: Member 1 of a です / じゃありません / ですか set built on one time, so the change is in the ending and nothing else.

items.target: さんじです
items.reviewNote: EXERCISES II model dialogue, B's reply. Split from ima-nanji-q. English is close to the existing ks1-ima-sanji ('It is 3:00 now.') and san-ji ('3:00, three o'clock'), so this card carries a hint; the owner may want to hint san-ji as well.
items.scene: answering what time it is now, without いま (ima)

items.target: いつですか
items.note: いつ (itsu) plus ですか (desu ka). Unlike なんじですか (nan-ji desu ka) it does not demand a clock time, so a day on its own answers it.
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: the whole question, where the book cards only the bare word いつ (itsu).

items.target: きょうのかいぎはなんじですか
items.pronunciation: kyō no kaigi wa nan-ji desu ka.
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: きょう (kyō) appears in exactly one sentence in the deck, and only as an answer. Also the deck's second-ever plain 〜はなんじですか question.
items.note: きょうの (kyō no) attaches the day to the noun after it, so は (wa) ends up marking the whole phrase きょうのかいぎ (kyō no kaigi) as the topic.

items.target: そうですか。どうもありがとう
items.reviewNote: SPEAKING PRACTICE 1, lifted verbatim — Sasaki's closing turn. Vocabulary job: そうですか (sō desu ka) and どうもありがとう (dōmo arigatō) exist as separate word cards but never as the single closing turn the dialogue actually uses, which is how the learner will need them.

items.target: いいえ、くじじゃありません
items.reviewNote: Constructed answer to ima-kuji-desu-ka, the negative reply. Form job: completes the yes/no pair on the いいえ、〜じゃありません shape from Lesson 1.
items.scene: answering no to whether it is 9:00 now

items.english: What time is it now in the UK?
items.target: イギリスはいまなんじですか
items.pronunciation: igirisu wa ima nanji desu ka
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-2) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: Built entirely from Lesson 3's clock vocabulary

items.target: スーパーはごごろくじまでです
items.pronunciation: sūpā wa gogo roku-ji made desu.
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle job: まで (made) as a standalone statement — the deck has that shape only for ジム; everywhere else まで arrives already wrapped inside a から〜まで sentence.

items.english: What time is it in London now?
items.target: ロンドンはいまなんじですか
items.pronunciation: rondon wa ima nan-ji desu ka.
items.reviewNote: SPEAKING PRACTICE 1 — a section with no cards at all. GRAMMAR 1 explicitly teaches that a geographical name is made the topic with は, and this was the only worked example of it. Quiz 1 item 2 tests this exact sentence. ロンドン comes from Lesson 1.
items.note: When you ask the time somewhere else, the place name becomes the topic with は (wa). Compare the plain いまなんじですか (ima nan-ji desu ka), which asks about where you are.

items.english: What time is happy hour, from and to?
items.target: ハッピーアワーはなんじからなんじまでですか
items.pronunciation: happī awā wa nan-ji kara nan-ji made desu ka.
items.reviewNote: Constructed from EXERCISES IV-C item 2 (ハッピーアワー, 4:00–7:00). Vocabulary job: ハッピーアワー (happī awā) is taught in the chapter vocabulary and used in no sentence.

items.target: ごぜんはちじはんです
items.reviewNote: SPEAKING PRACTICE 1, Nakamura's reply, split from london-ima-nanji-q. Also the deck's first sentence using ごぜん (gozen), which until now existed only as a bare word and in the bare time ごぜんよじ.
items.scene: answering what time it is in London

items.english: What time does the shop open?
items.target: みせはなんじからですか
items.pronunciation: mise wa nan-ji kara desu ka.
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: みせ (mise) is the first word of the chapter's vocabulary and appears in no sentence card at all. Built on the lesson's own 〜はなんじからですか frame from EXERCISES IV-A.

items.target: しごとはくじからです
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle job: から (kara) on its own with しごと, and the first half of a minimal pair with shigoto-goji-made in which only the particle changes.
items.note: Key Sentence 2, しごとはくじからごじまでです (shigoto wa ku-ji kara go-ji made desu), is this sentence with its closing half added.

items.target: ばんごはん
items.reviewNote: Duplicate of the established ばんごはん (bangohan) card in Lesson 8. The Lesson 3 sentences that use the word still teach it.
items.note: ばん (ban), evening, + ごはん (gohan), meal. Pairs with あさごはん (asagohan), breakfast.

items.target: よじからしちじまでです
items.reviewNote: Constructed answer to happii-awaa-q, using the book's own 4:00–7:00 cue. Elliptical, so it carries a hint naming the question.
items.scene: answering what hours happy hour runs

items.target: あさごはん
items.reviewNote: Duplicate of the established あさごはん (asagohan) card in Lesson 8. The Lesson 3 sentences that use the word still teach it.
items.note: あさ (asa), morning, + ごはん (gohan), meal — the same compounding as ひるやすみ (hiruyasumi) from this lesson.

items.english: What time is the last order?
items.target: ラストオーダーはなんじですか
items.pronunciation: rasuto ōdā wa nan-ji desu ka.
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue. The deck teaches なんじ (nan-ji) as vocabulary and the から/まで questions via fill-in-the-blank drills, but has no plain 〜はなんじですか sentence anywhere, which is the most basic use of the word.
items.note: Plain 〜はなんじですか asks the time an event happens. Use から (kara) or まで (made) instead when you want the start or the end of a stretch of time, as in ランチタイムはなんじからですか (ranchitaimu wa nan-ji kara desu ka).

items.target: にふん
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-2) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: Lesson 3 teaches the ...fun minute counter

items.target: ごぜんはちじからです
items.reviewNote: Constructed answer to puuru-nanji-kara-q, from the book's own 8:00 A.M. cue. Also only the second sentence anywhere in the deck to use ごぜん (gozen).
items.scene: answering what time the pool opens

items.english: What time does the meeting run from and until?
items.target: かいぎはなんじからなんじまでですか
items.pronunciation: kaigi wa nan-ji kara nan-ji made desu ka.
items.reviewNote: EXERCISES IV-C model dialogue, verbatim. The deck has this pattern once (fib-c3-lunch-break-q), so this is the second and last example. Quiz 1, part II item 4 asks the learner to produce exactly this pattern from scratch, so one worked example is thin.

items.target: ジムはごぜんくじからです
items.pronunciation: jimu wa gozen ku-ji kara desu.
items.reviewNote: Constructed from EXERCISES VI item 3 (ジム, 9:00 A.M.). Vocabulary job: the deck's only ジム sentence is a まで statement, so this topic had never been seen with から, and ごぜん (gozen) had never appeared in a statement.
items.note: Pairs with ジムはしちじまでです (jimu wa shichi-ji made desu): から (kara) gives the opening time, まで (made) the closing time, and the topic never changes.

items.target: あさのかいぎはくじからです
items.pronunciation: asa no kaigi wa ku-ji kara desu.
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: あさ (asa) is a card but is used nowhere except inside the compound あさごはん (asagohan). Puts it in the から frame the lesson already drills.
items.note: の (no) can hang a part of the day on a noun as well as on a clock time: あさのかいぎ (asa no kaigi) beside あしたのよじ (ashita no yo-ji) from Key Sentence 3.
